## What it is

A draft of the introduction section of your project, plus a data analysis plan and your dataset. The entire proposal should be about **1 page**. Use "Print Preview" to check the size of your .Rmd html output.

## Sections

**Section 1a: Description of dataset.** Cover:

- Where the dataset comes from, what interests you about it, and why you chose it.
- Its dimensions and variable names/types.
- What each row (observation) is.
- Whether the data seem "tidy".

**Section 1b: Data and data dictionary.** Place your data in the `/data` folder, and add the dimensions and a data dictionary to the README in that folder. Then print the output of `glimpse()` or `skim()` of your data frame.

**Section 2: Exploratory visualization.** Very preliminary exploratory data analysis, including some summary statistics and visualizations, along with some explanation of how they help you learn more about your data.

**Section 3: Pose a question and a potential method.** What question could you answer with this dataset, and which method(s) do you believe will help answer it? You can update these later as you work on your project.

## Grading (20 pts)

| Part | Points |
|---|---|
| Data | 6 |
| Proposal | 10 |
| Workflow, organization and code quality | 2 |
| Teamwork | 2 |
| **Total** | **20** |

After you receive feedback you can improve the proposal and re-submit. If you re-submit, your final score is the **average** of your first and second submissions.

## Tips for a strong proposal

- Keep it to about one page; focused beats exhaustive.
- Make sure your dataset meets the [dataset requirements](index.qmd#choosing-a-dataset) (at least 50 rows, at least 10 variables, a mix of variable types, loads into R).
- Each dataset page on this site has an "Explanation of data" section that can help you write Section 1a.
- Commit, push and open a pull request often, and share the writing fairly: teamwork is graded.
